text: Why nq "took hours" before [computer]. Not reproduced. gap/c4_q3.g now prints the wall time per stage. On the Modal container (GAP 4.14 from Debian trixie, nq from gap-nq), with the weight-5 commutators not passed to nq (Q3_NQTOP := false; they are redundant for class := 4, and they stay in the output relators): nq takes 4 s for the infinite Rd4, Rd6 and 132 s (Rf15, Rd46f15), 267 s (Rf16) for the finite ones — the large exponents $2^{15},2^{16}$ cost nq a factor 30–60, but minutes, not hours. The rest of GAP is the same for all: lower central series about 1 s, abelian invariants and the snf basis of $\gamma_4$ 30–43 s, exponents of the 540 commutators 8 s, and then about 570 s (90 % of GAP's CPU time) for the one remaining step, the check that the extra test word $w$ lies in $\gamma_4(M)$ and is nontrivial (MappedWord of a long word into the pcp group and membership in $\gamma_4$) — that, not nq, is what makes a base take 10 min (presumably also for the R2 bases above, whose logs have no stage times). Whether the hours in Docker came from the 3240 redundant relators given to nq for a finite group, or from the memory of the Docker VM, was not tested.

Summary of the first pass of class 4 [computer + on paper]: for each of the 80 bases $\Gamma$ of §6.6 and every $K\subseteq\gamma_4(M)$, $M=\Gamma/\gamma_5(\Gamma)\Gamma''$, the group $M/K$ has $D_7=1$ (P6, R, R2: 17 bases), $D_6=1$ (L: 7) or $D_5=1$ (T, S: 56). In particular no metabelian group of class 4 obtained from these presentations by a central modification of $\gamma_4$ has $D_7\ne1$; finding one needs a base $\Gamma$ outside this family.

text: The plateau is forced by the grading [on paper]. In the component of $a$ (degree 2) a word with $k$ letters $x_4$ has $2+Nk$ other letters, so its length is $2+(N+1)k\in\{2,\,N+3,\,2N+4,\dots\}$; the same holds for $L_N$ of [IMP26] with the grading $\deg x_5=(0,1)$, $\deg x_4=(0,-N)$, $\deg x_{1,2,3}=(1,0)$. Since $\varpi^n$ is spanned by the words of length $\ge n$, $\varpi^{N+4}\cap U(L)_2=\varpi^{2N+4}\cap U(L)_2$, hence $D_{N+4}\cap L_2=D_{2N+4}\cap L_2$: once $D_{N+4}\subseteq L_2$, the length $N+1$ of the plateau is the gap between the admissible lengths $N+3$ and $2N+4$. (Computed: for $N=2$ the component of $a$ in $A_6,A_7,A_8$ is the same 414 columns and 1 791 rows.) A group ring has no such grading: $\mu(x^E)-1=\sum_k\binom Eka^k$ mixes all lengths.

text: Lemma 5 [on paper] (Lemma 3 for $c=5$). (i) $\psi:A_5\to\Delta^5/\Delta^n$, $k\mapsto k-1$, is a homomorphism for $n\le10$: $kk'-1=(k-1)+(k'-1)+(k-1)(k'-1)$ and $(k-1)(k'-1)\in\Delta^{10}$. (ii) For $K\subseteq A_5$: $(K-1)A+\Delta^n=\Delta^n+\sum_k\psi(k)R$, $R=\mathrm{span}\{1\}\cup\{(x_{j_1}-1)\cdots(x_{j_l}-1):1\le l\le n-6\}$, $k$ over generators of $K$ ($K$ is central, $\psi(k)\Delta^{n-5}\subseteq\Delta^n$, and $\Delta/\Delta^{n-5}$ is spanned by these monomials). The proof is that of Lemma 3 with $4\to5$.
section: 6.10. MATH-43, class 5: all $K\subseteq\gamma_5(M)$ at once for the shifted plateau

text: Proposition 6 [on paper] (Proposition 4 for $c=5$). Let $U_n=J_n+\Lambda(A_5\otimes R_+)$, $R_+$ the monomials of degree $1..n-6$, $\bar\psi_n:A_5\to A/U_n$. If $\bar\psi_n$ is injective, then $D_n(M/K)\cap\gamma_5(M)/K=1$ for every $K\subseteq A_5$. Conversely every $v\in D_n(M/K)\cap A_5$, $v\notin K$, gives $1\ne vk^{-1}\in\ker\bar\psi_n$ for some $k\in K$, and $D_n(M)\cap A_5\subseteq\ker\bar\psi_n$. Further: $\ker\bar\psi_n$ is torsion ($z\in\ker\bar\psi_n$ gives $z-1\in\Delta^6$, so $z\in D_6(M)\subseteq\sqrt{\gamma_6(M)}=\tau(M)$, Jennings), so it is enough to test the elements of order 2 of $\tau(A_5)$; $\ker\bar\psi_{n+1}\subseteq\ker\bar\psi_n$ ($n+1\le10$); injectivity found modulo $2^{32}$ is exact. Proof: as for Proposition 4. For $n=6$, $R_+=\varnothing$ and $U_6=J_6$: the test is just $D_6(M)\cap\gamma_5$.
section: 6.10. MATH-43, class 5: all $K\subseteq\gamma_5(M)$ at once for the shifted plateau

text: Removing $\cap\,\gamma_5$ [on paper]. For $K\subseteq\gamma_5(M)$, $(M/K)/\gamma_5(M/K)=M/\gamma_5(M)=\Gamma/\gamma_5(\Gamma)\Gamma''=:Q$, a class-4 group that depends neither on $K$ nor on $\varphi$ (also $G/\gamma_5(G)=Q$). The image of $D_n(M/K)$ in $Q$ lies in $D_n(Q)$. So $$D_n(Q)=1\ \text{and}\ \bar\psi_n\ \text{injective}\ \Longrightarrow\ D_n(M/K)=1\ \text{for every}\ K\subseteq\gamma_5(M).$$ $D_8(Q)=1$ was not known: §6.8(a) is about the class-3 quotients of the class-4 bases, and §6.7 tested only $D_n(G)\cap\gamma_5$. Since $D_8(Q)\subseteq D_5(Q)$, it is enough to have $D_5(Q)=1$, and by Corollary 2 (with $Q_3=Q/\gamma_4(Q)=\Gamma/\gamma_4(\Gamma)\Gamma''$) that follows from $D_5(Q_3)=1$ (Lemma 1) and $D_5(Q)\cap\gamma_4(Q)=1$ (the map $\gamma_4(Q)\to\Delta^4/\Delta^5$ is additive and its kernel is torsion; the elements of order 2 must stay independent modulo $J_5(Q)$). A separate test, but a cheap one ($n=5$, $\dim A_5=780$).
